=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:_push_targets (lines 430-445 in diff) | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: A bare `git push origin HEAD` is treated as a push to a literal branch named `HEAD`, so the guard queries for a nonexistent PR branch instead of checking the current branch.
  WHY: A push from a branch whose PR has merged can bypass the merged-PR check and strand commits; reviewers rated this from MAJOR to BLOCKER, so the highest severity is used.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py: lines 316-348 in diff | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Assignment-prefix scanning recognizes `NAME=value` but not Bash append assignments such as `NAME+=value`, so a prefixed guarded git command can go undetected.
  WHY: The outer `git_subcommands()` scan can return early before the new guard logic runs, allowing a push to bypass the check; reviewers rated this from MAJOR to BLOCKER, so the highest severity is used.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py: lines 398-415 in diff | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `_push_targets` unconditionally slices `positionals[1:]`, dropping the only refspec when `--repo` or `--repo=` has already consumed the repository argument.
  WHY: The guard checks the current branch instead of the explicit destination, potentially allowing a push to a merged branch with no open PR.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:_shell_segments_with_operators / _push_targets | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Shell redirection operators are split as command separators, leaving file-descriptor digits such as `2` in the push arguments where they can be mistaken for refspecs and obscuring the effective working directory.
  WHY: The guard may check a nonexistent branch rather than the actual push destination, allowing a push that should be blocked or falsely blocking a valid push; reviewers rated this from NIT to BLOCKER, so the highest severity is used.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:_guarded_git_invocations (lines 284-290 in diff) | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Encountering `||` clears a working directory established by an earlier unconditional `cd`.
  WHY: The push runs from the worktree in Bash, but the guard evaluates it against the session checkout, which can cause false blocks or allow a push to a merged branch.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:_push_targets() / _evaluate_bash | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `git push --tags` produces no targets, so the guard performs no merged-PR check.
  WHY: A tag-only push from a merged-branch checkout is allowed without the check that previously examined the current branch.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:_push_targets() / _evaluate_bash | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: When an explicit source tip cannot be resolved, the fallback target discards the refspec's explicit destination and checks the session checkout's current branch instead.
  WHY: A push such as `git push origin nope:feature/x` can be judged by an unrelated clean branch rather than the named destination.

  confidence=[5]

- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:_branch_ref and _push_targets
  Line or code reference: _branch_ref (lines 380-394 in diff) and _push_targets refspec loop (lines 398-415 in diff)

  severity=MAJOR | confidence=4

  WHY: The push proceeds without commit/push subcommand detection or worktree-cwd resolution.

  severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When `--repo` consumes the repository argument, `refspecs = positionals[1:]` drops the remaining refspec.
  WHY: The guard checks the current branch instead of the explicit destination, which can allow a push to a merged branch.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:_push_targets
  Line or code reference: refspec parsing loop, redirection tokens end up in `positionals`
  severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The `2` from `2>&1` is treated as a positional argument and then as a refspec.
  WHY: The guard may issue an unnecessary PR lookup for branch `2`; the practical harm is minimal.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:_guarded_git_invocations
  Line or code reference: operator handling, lines 284-290 in diff
  severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `||` clears a working directory established by an earlier unconditional `cd`.
  WHY: A worktree push can be evaluated against the session checkout, causing a false block or a false allow.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "For git push <remote> HEAD:<ref> or <src>:<ref>, check the target ref (<ref>) for a merged PR with no open PR, not the local branch name. A detached HEAD pushing to an open PR's branch must be allowed."
  Expected change site: .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:_branch_ref and _push_targets
  Evidence of absence: The implementation correctly handles colon-separated refspecs like `HEAD:feature/open` and `feature/x:feature/x`. The detached-HEAD push to open PR is covered by `test_worktree_push_to_open_branch_from_merged_checkout`. However, the bare `HEAD` case (no colon) treats `HEAD` as a literal branch name rather than resolving it to the current branch at the effective working directory, which is a correctness bug reported above under SECURITY.
  severity=MAJOR | confidence=4

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py
  Line or code reference: _push_targets refspec parsing (source = destination = refspec; branch = _branch_ref(destination))
  severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `git push <remote> HEAD` is treated as a push to a literal branch named `HEAD` rather than the checked-out branch.
  WHY: The guard queries for PRs with head ref `HEAD`, finds none, and allows a push to an already-merged branch.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py
  Line or code reference: _push_targets argument parsing (refspecs = positionals[1:] if positionals else [])
  severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `--repo <remote>` or `--repo=<remote>` can leave only the refspec in `positionals`, but `_push_targets` drops it with `positionals[1:]`.
  WHY: The guard falls back to the checked-out branch and can miss a push to a merged destination.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py
  Line or code reference: _shell_segments_with_operators and _guarded_git_invocations operator checking
  severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Redirection characters are treated as command separators, resetting the working directory or leaving descriptor digits in the push arguments.
  WHY: The guard may fall back to the session checkout or treat `2` as a refspec, leading to incorrect blocking decisions.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py
  Line or code reference: _guarded_git_invocations operator handling
  severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `||` resets the working directory even when an earlier unconditional `cd` established it.
  WHY: A git command in the worktree can be evaluated against the session checkout and falsely blocked.

  severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5

- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py
  Line or code reference: _guarded_git_invocations, the assignment-prefix loop: `while index < len(tokens) and re.match(r"^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=", tokens[index]):`
  severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The assignment-prefix scanner misses Bash append assignments such as `NAME+=value`; the same regex in `git_subcommands()` also misses them.
  WHY: The outer scan can return before the new guard logic runs, allowing a guarded push to bypass the check.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py
  Line or code reference: _SHELL_PUNCTUATION_CHARS = ";&|\n<>"; _shell_segments_with_operators treats any token whose set is a subset of these chars as a separator
  severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The tokenizer treats `<` and `>` as command separators, splitting redirections from their command and potentially losing the worktree context.
  WHY: A push with redirection can be parsed incorrectly and evaluated against the wrong branch.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py
  Line or code reference: _push_targets() — `refspecs = positionals[1:] if positionals else []`
  severity=MAJOR | confidence=4

  WHY: The guard checks the current branch instead of the explicit destination and can allow a push to a merged branch.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py
  Line or code reference: _guarded_git_invocations operator handling — `if operator not in ("", "&&", ";", "\n"): working_directory = None`
  severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The parser drops a working directory established by an earlier unconditional `cd` when it encounters `||`.
  WHY: A worktree push can be evaluated against the session checkout, causing a false positive or false negative.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py
